question: How many numbers up to 200 are divisible by 4 and 3 both?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers divisible by both 4 and 3 ⇒ divisible by LCM(4,3) = 12

Count = 200 ÷ 12 = 16 (ignore remainder)

**∴ Answer = 16**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Find numbers ≤ 200 divisible by both 4 and 3

**Formula used:**

Count = N ÷ LCM(a, b)

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 4 and 3 = 12

⇒ Numbers divisible by 12 up to 200

⇒ 200 ÷ 12 = 16.66

⇒ Taking integer part ⇒ 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Concept

Common divisibility uses LCM.

Counting Formula

Count = ⌊N / divisor⌋

Divisibility Rule

If divisible by LCM ⇒ divisible by each number.
